title: Autonomous MBots
summary: Research work on how mobile robots move, and how to make that behavior safer.
overview: My work with MBots focused on motion analysis and real-time safety. I used wheel encoder data to examine velocity and acceleration accuracy, and analyzed the results to better understand how the robots behaved over time in a practical setting.
This was part of my research work in the MARVL Lab. I helped with computer vision and the lower level state estimation used to inspect and discuss robot motion relative to their environment.

photo.alt: A wheeled MBot with a LiDAR scanner and other onboard electronics on an outdoor table.

title: Handwritten Character Recognition
summary: Comparing two kinds of neural networks on handwritten English characters.
overview: For this project, I compared feedforward and convolutional neural networks on handwritten English characters using Julia. I trained the models with the handwritten character dataset by Cohen, Afshar, Tapson, and van Schaik.
I looked at accuracy, confusion matrices, and learning curves to understand which characters each model recognized well and where it struggled.

photo.alt: A handwritten R alongside neural-network outputs; the predicted label is R.

title: 3D Mapping from LiDAR Data
summary: Using Julia to bring separate LiDAR scans together into a 3D map.
overview: I used Julia to combine separate LiDAR scans into a 3D map. Each scan captured the scene from a different angle, so the project involved processing the point clouds and aligning them in a shared coordinate frame.
The resulting visualization let me inspect how the scans fit together and spot problems in the alignment.

title: Orbital Satellite Simulation
summary: Using a ground robot to study aspects of satellite motion.
overview: In the VODCA Lab, I helped develop a satellite orbit simulation using an omnidirectional ground rover as a physical testing metric. My work was specifically in the lower-level control between the simulated models and physical robots that supported real-time data collection and analysis.
The goal was to simulate the theoretical orbital motion of a satellite in a controlled lab space, within the limits of what a the MBots can represent.

photo.alt: An omnidirectional rover with three roller wheels and onboard electronics.

title: Auction Notification System
summary: A Python tool that watches auction listings and sends alerts for matching items.
overview: I built this Python tool to keep track of online auctions without repeatedly checking listings by hand. It collects listings, filters them by details such as keywords and price, and sends a notification when an item matches.
The project brought together web scraping, APIs, and an alert workflow, with retries and rate limiting to handle changes in the listing sources.

title: Quadplane Development
summary: Working on an aircraft that combines vertical takeoff with fixed-wing flight.
overview: I contributed to work on a hybrid aircraft that combines a quadcopter’s vertical takeoff with fixed-wing flight capabilities. The project involved flight-control logic, hardware integration, and most primarily testing how the aircraft behaved in different operating modes.
The project featured different modalities where the quadplane would function between a simulated circular motion and controlled flight
